governor.label: Xavier Becerra (D)
paragraphs: Healthcare: strengthen Medi-Cal and build toward universal single-payer coverage; make care affordable without debt or delays.
Housing and living costs: build more affordable homes; challenge price gouging and unjustified rate hikes; expand help with childcare.
Energy and federal policy: invest in clean energy and grid resilience, with benefits for renters and low-income households; oppose Trump administration actions he says harm California.

governor.label: Steve Hilton (R)
paragraphs: Energy: proposes eliminating the state gasoline excise tax, gasoline cap-and-trade costs and the Low Carbon Fuel Standard, easing refinery rules and increasing California oil production. His $3-per-gallon target is a campaign projection, not a verified outcome.
Taxes and housing: proposes eliminating state income tax for people/families earning under $150,000 and reducing development fees and environmental regulations.

Spending: proposes ending high-speed rail, reducing state government jobs and ending healthcare coverage for undocumented Californians. The last two paragraphs summarize KQED reporting, not an official fiscal estimate.

lieutenant-governor.label: Fiona Ma (D)
paragraphs: Higher education: make college more affordable, expand paid internships and strengthen career pathways.
Economy and administration: reduce red tape for housing and small businesses; emphasize financial accountability, transparency and cutting waste.

lieutenant-governor.label: Gloria Romero (R)
paragraphs: Education: restore academic standards, expand parental choice and defend her interpretation of Title IX protections for girls in sports; fight antisemitism on campuses.

Economy and government: promote business growth, reduce bureaucracy and restrain commissions she says have failed to protect water and farmland. Her statement does not give a costed implementation plan.

secretary-of-state.label: Shirley Weber (D)
paragraphs: Voting access: protect vote-by-mail and access to the ballot; oppose shorter polling hours and fewer voting days.
Election administration: defend eligible voters’ rights and protect election officials from threats; emphasize transparent administration.

secretary-of-state.label: Don Wagner (R)
paragraphs: Election administration: speed ballot counting, update voter rolls and seek a nonpartisan Secretary of State office.

Election security: advocates photo identification at the polls and stronger eligibility checks. His allegations about current election failures are campaign claims, not findings adopted by this guide.

controller.label: Malia Cohen (D)
paragraphs: Financial oversight: expand public access to financial and payroll data, provide timely cash reports and promote accurate local-government reporting.
Operations: modernize state payroll and return unclaimed property. These are the priorities and record described in her statement.

controller.label: Herb Morgan (R)
paragraphs: Transparency: publish all state expenditures in an easy-to-use database with transaction-level detail and near-real-time reporting.
Audits: use pre-audits, expenditure review and post-audits to check performance and proper use of public funds.

treasurer.label: Eleni Kounalakis (D)
paragraphs: Public investment: use public finance to build more affordable housing and invest in the financial future of children and families.
Financial stewardship: protect pensions and responsibly manage state finances; defend healthcare and immigrant communities. The statement does not specify the mechanisms for all of these goals.

treasurer.label: Jennifer Hawks (R)
paragraphs: Oversight: demand transparency and measurable results in the management of taxpayer money; expose waste, fraud and mismanagement.
Investing: advocate responsible investment and independent financial oversight. She notes that the Treasurer cannot rewrite the budget or create laws.

attorney-general.label: Rob Bonta (D)
paragraphs: Public safety: defend gun-safety laws, expand violence prevention and pursue gun, drug and human trafficking organizations.
Rights and services: defend healthcare and reproductive freedom, enforce civil rights and protect immigrant communities.
Economic enforcement: pursue consumer fraud, wage theft and polluters. This summarizes his campaign issues page; the state guide contains no Bonta statement.

attorney-general.label: Michael Gates (R)
paragraphs: Public safety: fully enforce Proposition 36 on repeat theft and drug offenses; prosecute fentanyl traffickers and protect victims.

Homelessness and accountability: move people from the streets into treatment and ensure tax dollars are spent effectively. Crime statistics and claimed past results in his statement are not independently verified here.

insurance-commissioner.label: Ben Allen (D)
paragraphs: Insurance market: increase competition and insurance options rather than create a new large-scale public insurance system; oppose unfair nonrenewals.
Claims and disaster recovery: make claims faster and fairer, increase transparency, support wildfire-risk reduction and speed rebuilding.

insurance-commissioner.label: Jane Kim (D)
paragraphs: Public insurance: establish a public Disaster Insurance for All program, using premiums to make communities safer.
Consumer protection: cap excessive profits, investigate illegal price-fixing and make claims fast and fair; seek guaranteed healthcare for every California child.

boe-d2.label: Sally Lieber (D)
paragraphs: Property taxes: support accurate, equitable assessments and expand taxpayer assistance and access to relief, including for veterans and low-income households.
Housing and recovery: support affordability and rapid disaster recovery; uphold Proposition 13 and insist wealthy interests pay taxes owed.

boe-d2.label: John Pimentel (D)
paragraphs: Tax reform: advocate ending sales tax on restaurant and delivered food and closing tax loopholes for billionaires and corporations.
BOE oversight: improve consistency and transparency in property assessments and scrutinize utility tax treatment. The food-tax proposal would require action beyond the Board’s assessment role.

superintendent-public-instruction.label: Richard Barrera
paragraphs: Schools: direct more resources to classrooms, improve reading and math, and expand college and career readiness.
Student protection: keep ICE out of schools, protect LGBTQ students, support vaccination and improve campus safety infrastructure.

superintendent-public-instruction.label: Sonja Shaw
paragraphs: Academics and spending: restore high standards in reading, writing and math, reduce bureaucracy and make school spending transparent.
Parents and Title IX: advocate a stronger parent role and her interpretation of protections for girls’ sports and private spaces.

ca-11.label: Connie Chan (D)
paragraphs: Healthcare and families: reverse federal healthcare cuts, pass Medicare for All, and expand affordable childcare and free community college nationwide.
Housing and immigration: expand federal housing programs for working people; abolish ICE and pass immigration reform.
Taxes and foreign policy: require billionaires and large corporations to pay more fairly; end corruption and push to end U.S. involvement in wars.

ca-11.label: Scott Wiener (D)
paragraphs: Housing and transit: pass national housing legislation, expand federal transit funding and shorten transit project delivery.
Healthcare and families: pass Medicare for All and national paid family leave.
Accountability: restrict ICE agents’ anonymity, ban congressional stock trading and remove dark money from elections.

ca-15.label: Kevin Mullin (D)
paragraphs: Democracy: protect voting-by-mail and advance anti-corruption and voting-rights legislation.
Economy and services: oppose federal cuts to safety-net programs; support consumer and worker protections, life sciences and clean energy.

Climate and immigration: prepare communities for climate change and oppose the administration’s immigration enforcement approach. Only Mullin submitted a statement in the SF pamphlet; that does not establish there is no ballot opponent.

ad-17.label: Matt Haney (D)
paragraphs: Housing: reduce approval barriers, convert vacant offices into homes and protect renters; his statement cites the one-month security-deposit cap.
Health and recovery: expand addiction treatment, mobile pharmacies, overdose prevention and recovery housing.
City services: support downtown recovery, transit, public schools and reproductive and mental healthcare. A sole pamphlet statement does not prove a candidate is unopposed.

ad-19.label: Catherine Stefani (D)
paragraphs: Safety: strengthen gun-safety enforcement, support crime victims and hold fentanyl dealers accountable.
Affordability and health: expand affordable housing, prevent homelessness and improve access to reproductive and other healthcare.
Energy: support offshore wind development. Only Stefani’s statement is included here; check the official ballot for any other candidate.

board-of-education.label: Autumn Brown Garibay
paragraphs: Literacy and math: every child reading by third grade and doing grade-level math by eighth grade.
Schools and budget: stable principals and teaching teams, safe classrooms, public budget scrutiny and spending tied to student outcomes.

board-of-education.label: Virginia Cheung
paragraphs: Early intervention: improve literacy, math, attendance and engagement before students fall behind.
Governance: restore fiscal accountability, rebuild family trust and ensure students feel safe and heard.

board-of-education.label: Alida Fisher
paragraphs: Instruction and inclusion: rigorous academics, early intervention, inclusive special education and meaningful support for families.
Governance: financial stability, modern financial/HR systems, school facilities, educator benefits and collaboration with labor.

board-of-education.label: Ryan Hazelton
paragraphs: Enrollment: reform the assignment lottery and expand wrap-around family services.
School operations: fair, timely educator pay; reduce absenteeism; fix the budget and seek more state funding; make schools welcoming to LGBTQ, immigrant and disabled students.

board-of-education.label: Phil Kim
paragraphs: Classrooms: support teachers and direct resources to the students who need them.
Governance: educator-informed decisions on curriculum and instruction, clear direction and stable schools. His statement gives broad priorities rather than a detailed new policy plan.

board-of-education.label: Laurance Lee
paragraphs: Schools: strong neighborhood schools, reading support and support for teachers; cites his work restoring eighth-grade Algebra 1.
Oversight: explain Board decisions, listen to families and scrutinize school construction spending.

board-of-education.label: Reina Tello
paragraphs: Community representation: bring SFUSD parent and former-student perspectives to Board decisions and uphold San Francisco values.

Policy-detail gap: her official statement emphasizes experience and endorsements but gives no specific budget, curriculum or assignment-system proposals. This is not evidence she has no positions elsewhere.

board-of-education.label: Tim Tung
paragraphs: Finances: protect a balanced budget and demand transparent performance data.
Enrollment and learning: deliver improvements to the student assignment system, reading and math; tie school investment to tangible results.

community-college-full.label: Elijah Ball
paragraphs: Planning: increase enrollment, modernize facilities and create long-term financial stability.
Governance: use a coordinated campus plan that serves students and faculty.

community-college-full.label: Rome Moses Jones
paragraphs: Student success: expand opportunity and strengthen support systems so students can reach their goals.
Policy-detail gap: the statement describes mentoring and service experience but does not offer a specific budget or course-restoration plan.

community-college-full.label: Monroe Lace
paragraphs: Core priorities: balance the budget, increase enrollment and put student success first.
Pathways: strengthen City College partnerships with K-12 schools and support degree, trade and lifelong-learning routes.

community-college-full.label: Leah LaCroix
paragraphs: Courses and enrollment: offer the classes students need and grow enrollment sustainably.
Governance: stabilize the Board, plan beyond crisis management and strengthen public input and oversight.

community-college-full.label: Jeremy Lee
paragraphs: Programs: strengthen Cantonese instruction and protect Free City College.
Finances and jobs: secure the college’s long-term finances and expand its role in workforce training and the local economy.

community-college-full.label: Bunny McFadden
paragraphs: Access: maintain the promise of free, open community college for San Franciscans at every life stage.
Policy-detail gap: her statement stresses the value of education and her teaching/workforce background but does not specify a new budget or enrollment plan.

community-college-full.label: Erwin Tam
paragraphs: Finances: reduce waste, develop long-term financial strategies and protect accreditation and essential services.
Students and staff: safe learning facilities, stable wages and benefits, and a financially viable college. His closure warning is a campaign claim, not a finding of this guide.

community-college-full.label: Lisa Palagi Wynn II
paragraphs: Policy-detail gap: the official statement lists education, behavioral-health commission service and student organizing, but no clear implementable policy platform.
The statement’s reference to “Prop 2” is not explained; this guide does not infer which proposal it means or attribute additional positions.

community-college-partial.label: Ruth Ferguson
paragraphs: Access: protect Free City, grow enrollment and keep college affordable for degree and job-training students.
Finances and governance: maintain a balanced budget, restore funding and incorporate student, faculty and staff priorities.

bart-d8.label: Sara Barz
paragraphs: Service: reliable trains, clean and safe stations, and working elevators, escalators and fare gates.
Access and oversight: welcoming accessible station plazas, better connections and transfers, and implementation of independent auditors’ cost-saving and transparency recommendations.

assessor-recorder.label: Joaquín Torres
paragraphs: Public service: modernize property-assessment systems and online records, shorten waits and improve help with exemptions.
Fairness: equitable assessments and appeals, estate-planning resources for families and easier nonprofit access to qualifying exemptions.

public-defender.label: Mano Raju
paragraphs: Defense: high-quality constitutional representation, with immigration, mental-health, youth and post-conviction services.
Root causes: record-clearing, better-paid and more diverse juries, youth programs, education and job pathways; pair social services with defense.

supervisor-d6.label: Matt Dorsey
paragraphs: Recovery: align city drug policy with long-term recovery; expand addiction medications and recovery-oriented supportive housing.
Neighborhoods: expand housing and office conversions, support renters and downtown recovery, and improve public and traffic safety.

supervisor-d6.label: Alex Behrend
paragraphs: Housing enforcement: use existing criminal penalties against landlords who unlawfully neglect building repairs.
Workers: enforce criminal laws against corporations to protect wages and working conditions; emphasize representation independent of billionaire and corporate backing.
